honing_confound: Shock skill damage scales with Specialization (gear-honing indexed). Shock Training tier standing reflects T4 meta where Shock skill burst output is valued.

delivery.evidence: Scrapper uses fist + cannon arm attacks. Shock skills (Thunder Dive, Hammer of Destruction, Battering Fists, Rolling Smash) are the primary Shock Training output — heavy hitting frontal attacks.

footprint.evidence: Shock skills hit in frontal cones and small-radius impacts. Rolling Smash creates a small AoE at target. Heavier-hitting than Wardancer but narrower AoE.

geo_text: Shock Training Scrapper: heavy melee brawler identity. Stamina fills from Stamina skills (green) and depletes from Shock skills (blue). In Shock Training identity, Shock skills deal significantly more damage. The rhythm is: build Stamina via green skills → spend Stamina on blue Shock skills for burst output.

control.evidence: Shock skills typically have high Stagger ratings (Hammer of Destruction = high stagger). Some knock enemies back. Stagger is a rider on damage identity — Scrapper is noted for Stagger contribution to raids.

defense.evidence: Scrapper is the tankier of the two MA subclasses (heavier build). Moderate mobility with dodge skills. Not as mobile as Wardancer.

economy.resource_verbatim: Stamina (fills via Stamina skills) and Shock (depletes via Shock skills); separate dual meters
economy.builder_source: GREEN skills (Stamina type) fill Stamina meter. BLUE skills (Shock type) consume Stamina from the meter.
economy.plain_text: DUAL METER: Two separate gauges — Stamina and Shock. Stamina gauge fills from casting Stamina-type (green) skills. Shock-type (blue) skills consume Stamina gauge AND generate Shock gauge. Full Shock gauge (from Z) grants a Shock buff. SHOCK TRAINING IDENTITY: Shock skills deal significantly more damage. The economy reward is spending Stamina on Shock skills as quickly as possible for sustained Shock output. The two-meter system creates a mandatory alternation between green and blue skill sets.

element.evidence: Scrapper's shock theme is lightning-physical. Heavy fist attacks with electric shock aesthetics.

movement.evidence: Moderate mobility. Some Shock skills include brief forward movement. Slower than Wardancer overall.

attr.evidence: All melee. Fist + cannon arm attacks require point-blank engagement.

range.evidence: Melee range for all Shock and Stamina skills.

tempo.evidence: Shock Training creates a build (Stamina via green skills) → spend (Shock skills) rhythm. The burst windows are the Shock skill sequences.

amp.value: Shock skills: significantly increased damage (Shock Training identity bonus); Shock gauge fill provides additional buff
amp.evidence: Training knowledge. Exact percentage not confirmed from live sources in this session.

commitment.evidence: Heavy Shock skills (Hammer of Destruction, Rolling Smash) have pronounced wind-up animations.

mechanics_notes: 1) Scrapper's dual-meter system (Stamina + Shock) is the most explicit alternation economy in LA: you MUST use green skills to have blue skill access, and vice versa. The class literally cannot sustain Shock skill output without Stamina investment. This creates a mandatory skill variety requirement. 2) HIGH STAGGER CONTRIBUTION: Scrapper is valued in raids for stagger damage (boss phase breaks). Hammer of Destruction is one of the highest stagger skills in the game. This utility function (non-damage but raid-valuable) is not captured in the delivery/control schema. 3) Shock Training emphasizes Specialization while Taijutsu emphasizes Swiftness — the stat distributions create different play feels (slower/harder-hitting Shock vs faster/combo-oriented Taijutsu). 4) Scrapper is the bulkier female martial artist vs Wardancer's speed — their respective 'weight' classes contrast directly and make for a good pair comparison in the corpus.
stabilization_patch: Shock Training has fluctuated in meta standing; Taijutsu has been dominant in several patches.
tier_standing_release: B-tier at launch (Taijutsu slightly preferred initially)
tier_standing_current: B/C-tier. HONING-CONFOUND NOTE: Shock skill burst output is Specialization-dependent; at high gear, Shock Training burst is competitive but Taijutsu's sustained output is often preferable in mobile raid environments.

honing_confound: Taijutsu's Swiftness dependency means attack speed and cast frequency scale with gear; at higher tiers, the rapid cycling advantage compounds. Tier standing reflects sustained-output advantage at T4 uptime.

delivery.evidence: Same fist+arm skill pool. Taijutsu emphasizes Normal skills (green) — the Stamina-type rapid combo skills — over Shock skills.

footprint.evidence: Normal skills are faster but narrower footprint than Shock skills. Rapid combo hits at melee range.

geo_text: Taijutsu Scrapper: rapid-combo sustained identity. Normal skills are enhanced — the fast green-skill combos become the primary DPS output. Shock skills are used less. The identity removes Shock gauge management complexity for a simpler but sustained fast-combo style.

control.evidence: Taijutsu skills also contribute Stagger, though less than Shock Training's high-stagger skills. The contribution is lower but still present.

economy.resource_verbatim: Normal skills on cooldown (Stamina/Shock meter still present but emphasis shifts)
economy.builder_source: N/A — Taijutsu shifts economy from meter management to cooldown cycling. Normal skills fire rapidly via high Swiftness investment.
economy.plain_text: COOLDOWN EMPHASIS: Taijutsu simplifies the dual-meter into a more cooldown-like economy by emphasizing Normal skills (which generate Stamina freely) and deprioritizing Shock skill expenditure. The class feels more like a 'fire everything as it cools down' identity than a 'manage two gauges' identity. Taijutsu engraving: Normal skill damage significantly increased; removes or simplifies the Shock gauge dependency.

movement.evidence: High Swiftness means faster attack speed and slightly faster movement. More mobile feel than Shock Training Scrapper.

tempo.evidence: Taijutsu is the sustained identity: no Shock-skill burst windows, just continuous Normal skill cycling.

amp.value: Normal skills: significantly increased damage (Taijutsu identity bonus)
amp.evidence: Training knowledge. The flat Normal skill boost parallels FI Wardancer's flat bonus structure.

commitment.evidence: Normal skills (green) are faster casts than Shock skills. Taijutsu emphasizes these faster animations.

mechanics_notes: 1) Taijutsu Scrapper parallels First Intention Wardancer in structure: remove the complex gauge-spending system (Shock gauge emphasis) and add a flat damage bonus to the 'simpler' skill track. Both are 'pure technique without the power-enhancement gimmick' identities. 2) Taijutsu is generally MORE POPULAR than Shock Training in 2024-2026 meta due to better uptime on mobile bosses — sustained fast combo doesn't require positioning for slow heavy Shock skills. 3) The two Scrapper identities (Shock Training = heavy burst vs Taijutsu = fast sustained) are one of the clearest 'SLOW BIG HIT vs FAST SMALL HIT' identity pairs in LA. Good corpus pair for this dimension.
stabilization_patch: Taijutsu has been generally preferred since 2023.
tier_standing_current: A/B-tier. HONING-CONFOUND NOTE: Swiftness dependency means Taijutsu improves relatively at higher honing tiers where Swiftness stat budget expands.
